SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY AND QUARTELY INVESTMENT
  ACTIVITY REPORTS FOR JUNE 2023

ISSUE
Receive and file the monthly and quarterly investment activity reports for June 2023.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the monthly and quarterly
investment activity reports for City of Palmdale and Successor Agency for June 2023.

BACKGROUND
Pursuant to Section 16 of the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency Investment
Policy, the City Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on
investments to the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors. The
reports shall detail the type of investment, name of the issuer, purchase date, date of
maturity, amount of deposit, and rate of interest. This information shall be provided for
all City and Successor Agency pooled investments, as well as for Certificates of
Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts and
Community Facilities District accounts which are managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly reports provide a synopsis of the investment activity for the City of Palmdale
and Successor Agency. The reports provide information on assets, allocations, average
maturities, yields, and book valuations.
The interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report.

The market values presented for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are
based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This
information was obtained from the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets,
Capital Market Finances, or other reliable source of market prices.

DISCUSSION
Compliance with Investment Policy

For June, the invested portfolio amount for the City of Palmdale totaled $325,705,581,
an increase of $20,294,233 from the previous month, and an increase of $54,790,463
in comparison to last year. The monthly increase is the result of a combination of new
investment purchase, interest gains, and LAIF deposits.

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of June was $14,587,215. The balance
increased by $4,390,218 from last month due to a combination of cash deposit received
from LA County property taxes and earned interest.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs, Corporate
Notes, U.S. Treasury Securities and Government Agency Paper, each adhering to
portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entity’s investment policy to 1)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations; 2) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient liquidity
to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash requirements; and
3) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on, is providing liquidity to measure up
to the City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the Finance
Department is currently investing in two pooled funds, LAIF and CAMP. These are
intended for the daily operational activities, used for economic uncertainties and
maintenance needs. The pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the City
and Successor Agency meet cash flow requirements.

The total LAIF balance for the City of Palmdale at the end of June is $150,390,432, an
increase of $25,000,000 compared to the prior month, due to a deposit made by the
City’s general bank to LAIF.

Successor Agency LAIF balance at the end of June was $12,988,812. An increase of
$8,500,000 due to a transfer from Successor Agency cash account to the LAIF account.

CAMP’s balance for City of Palmdale at the end of June was $259,310 compared to
May balance of $258,197. The slight increase is due to interest earned during the month.

The interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report. As of June 30, 2023, the interest rates for LAIF and CAMP investments were at
3.167 percent and 5.24 percent, respectively. By comparison, the LAIF and CAMP
interest rates at the end of May were at 2.993 percent and 5.16 percent. Both rates have
slightly increased within this month. This time last year, LAIF and CAMP rates were at
0.861 percent and 1.14, respectively.

We anticipate that rates will remain fairly consistent, increasing only in small
percentages in the upcoming months, considering the history in the past year and the
current state of economy. CAMP shows better performance than LAIF in interest rates.
The difference between the performance of the two funds is partly due to the varying
pool characteristics. CAMP’s portfolio composition is much more subject to market
volatility, resulting in performance variation.

Diversity

The Finance Division aims to diversify the investment portfolios to avoid incurring
unreasonable and avoidable risks regarding specific security types or individual financial
institutions.

City of Palmdale and Successor Agency’s investment portfolios remain strongly
diversified. The monthly and quarterly reports include all investments held by both
entities and current book values as of June 30, 2023.

It is anticipated that both the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency will have sufficient
moneys to meet its expenditure requirements for the next 6 months as we continue to
monitor any financial impact due to the Coronavirus pandemic and the current economic
conditions and the impact on interest rates.

Attached are summaries of the investments in the City of Palmdale and Successor

ISSUE
Approve First Amendment for Agreement with Taft Electric Company to increase
contract price by $180,000 for an amount not to exceed $270,000 for a term through
June 2025.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve First Amendment for Agreement No. A-7526 with Taft Electric Company
  to increase contract price by $180,000 for an amount not to exceed $270,000.

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or their designee, to execute the First Amendment
  to Agreement No. A-7526 with Taft Electric Company including non-substantive
  changes.

BACKGROUND
The City released Invitation for Bid No. 20-001-3400 for As Needed Electrical Services
and/or Repairs in 2021 and awarded contracts to Taft Electric Company and M. Brey
Electric, Inc., in the total amount of $90,000 each through June 2025.

During the contract timeline, staff worked with both contractors and Taft Electric Company
has provided the most responsive and best quality of work for electrical service needs
required by the City’s Maintenance Division. Due to this, Taft Electric’s original contract
amount is being exhausted. Therefore, additional funds are required to continue
contracting the work under Taft Electric Company.

DISCUSSION
This amendment to increase the contract price, for Taft Electric Company, reflects the
needs for electrical services required by the Maintenance Division. Due to limited in
house resources, more electrical work is being contracted out, with estimates of
approximately $90,000 per year through June 2025. Some examples of contracted
electrical services include:

Facility Maintenance
   Replacement of hazardous lighting poles in City parks and parking lots identified
  in annual pole inspections.
   As needed lighting repairs throughout City parks and buildings for the safety of
  staff and the public.
   Emergency lighting pole repairs due to storm and wind damage.

Landscape Maintenance (General Benefit and Assessment Districts)
   Replacement of corroded electric meter pedestals.
   Replacement of traffic collision damaged electric meter pedestals.
   Replacement of traffic collision damaged irrigation controller/enclosures.
   Irrigation controller/enclosure replacements and electrical system upgrades.
   Upgrades to the Landscape and Park Maintenance team office space with
  additional PC network ports and conduit runs to server room.

Park Maintenance and Transit Services
   Maintenance shop and irrigation electrical circuit improvements at City parks.
   Booster and storm water pump electrical system maintenance.
   Central irrigation control network electrical upgrades.
   Conduit runs for ethernet in City parks.

FISCAL IMPACT
Sufficient funds for as needed electrical repairs and services are budgeted in Facility
Maintenance (10133005); Park Maintenance (10133002); Landscape Maintenance –
General Benefit (10133003); Landscape Maintenance – Assessment Districts
(25133003); and Transit Services (20333005) Contract Services accounts.
